title: Stewed Saltfish
subtitle: Caribbean salt cod simmered with tomato, pepper, and thyme
excerpt: Flaked salt cod cooked down in a fragrant sauce of tomato, onion, scotch bonnet, and thyme. A staple across the Caribbean, typically eaten at breakfast or brunch with boiled ground provisions or fried dumplings.
sourceNotes: Eaten across the Caribbean from Jamaica to Trinidad. Salt cod arrived with the colonial trade in preserved fish and has remained central to the region's cooking.

recipe.freezeNotes: Salt cod dishes do not freeze well; the texture of the fish becomes rubbery on defrosting.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The stew holds well in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat gently with a splash of water.

content.text: Stewed saltfish is a Caribbean salt cod dish cooked in a tomato and pepper sauce. Soak the cod for at least 12 hours and change the water twice to draw out the salt. If it still tastes very salty after soaking, boil it once more in fresh water before using.

items.prepNote: soaked in cold water for 12 to 24 hours, water changed twice

content.text: Drain the soaked salt cod. Put it in a large saucepan, cover with fresh cold water, and bring to the boil. Simmer for 15 minutes. Drain and leave to cool slightly.
Remove any skin and bones from the cooked fish. Break the flesh into large flakes with your fingers and set aside.
Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Fry both onions for 6 minutes until they soften. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add both peppers and cook for 3 minutes. Stir in the tomato puree.
Add the chopped tomatoes, whole scotch bonnet, thyme sprigs, allspice berries, and 100 ml of water. Stir and bring to a simmer.
Add the flaked salt cod and spring onions. Fold gently to combine. Cook on medium-low heat for 10 minutes, stirring carefully so the fish stays in flakes.
Remove the scotch bonnet, thyme sprigs, and allspice berries. Taste and season with black pepper. Salt may not be needed. Serve with boiled yam, fried dumplings, or rice.

items.symptom: The fish is still very salty after soaking and boiling.
items.cause: The soaking time was too short, or the water was not changed.
items.fix: Drain the cooking water, cover with fresh water, and boil for a further 10 minutes. Taste again before adding to the sauce.

items.symptom: The fish breaks into very small pieces.
items.fix: Fold it in gently and avoid stirring more than needed. Use a wide spatula or spoon rather than a wooden spoon.

items.cause: The scotch bonnet broke apart during cooking.
items.fix: Use a very fresh, intact scotch bonnet. Check it often and remove it as soon as it begins to soften and the skin shows signs of splitting.
